title: Rust: directional RF and fixed-profile signaling
description:
Publish and adopt the wire.12 directional evidence contract through rust/lichen-rpl/src/message.rs, rust/lichen-core/src/sf_assignment.rs and rust/lichen-node/src/scheduler.rs. Retain authenticated receiver/direction/channel/profile/time/coverage/validity. Scheduled profile 0x01 remains fixed SF10; stale/unknown evidence, reverse-link SNR, queue load, end-to-end timeout and CCA exhaustion cannot authorize a PHY transition.

HPC8 execution policy: Code, test, or schema changes require three independent correctness, security, and robustness reviews; file and fix all findings and re-review. Use independent oracles, never weakened legacy tests or self-generated expected results. Preserve upstream Yggdrasil addressing, radio-owned identity, best-effort custody, baseline SCHC, and the human-only OSCORE/EDHOC security edit bar. External actions, hardware/RF operations, and port access require scoped explicit permission and applicable bench safety checks. Research may conclude no-go; an authorization gate requires affirmative, recorded approval for its actual scope. Dependency closure and decomposition are not permission. No speculative activation, including deferred portability or experimental modes.
design: This is the Rust CCP2 slice of b7z9.74. rust.02 owns the generic wire boundary; reuse it rather than implement another codec. b7z9.71's closure only establishes its C emission slice and is not Rust conformance or permission for load-based SF allocation. Do not add adaptive PHY behavior, key portability, new signature domains or audited OSCORE/EDHOC changes.
acceptance_criteria: Use independent vectors.02/.07 through production publication, decoding and profile policy. Verify exact bytes, report ownership, asymmetric directions, expiry, unsupported/unconfirmed transitions and unchanged receiver channel/SF under repeated congestion. Exercise core/RPL/node signaling tests using manifest-supported hosted features and relevant no_std checks. Run fmt and clippy. Preserve legacy SF-assignment tests and never reinterpret an absent legacy field as CCP2 admission.
